User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the TravelWise application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user entity.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user account was created.

Trip.title: Trip
Trip.description: Represents a travel trip planned by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the trip entity.

userId.description: Reference to User. (Relationship: User 1:N Trip). The ID of the user who created the trip.

startDate.description: The start date of the trip.

endDate.description: The end date of the trip.

destinations.description: An array of destinations included in the trip.

totalCost.description: The total estimated cost of the trip.

shareId.description: A unique ID used for sharing the trip.

sharedWith.description: References to Users. (Relationship: User N:N Trip). An array of user IDs with whom the trip is shared.

isPublic.description: Indicates whether the trip is publicly accessible.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the trip was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the trip was last updated.

days.description: An array of Day objects, representing the itinerary for each day of the trip.

Day.title: Day
Day.description: Represents a single day within a trip itinerary.

id.description: Unique identifier for the day entity.

tripId.description: Reference to Trip. (Relationship: Trip 1:N Day) The ID of the trip to which this day belongs.

activities.description: References to Activity. (Relationship: Day 1:N Activity) An array of activity IDs planned for the day.

Activity.title: Activity
Activity.description: Represents a single activity within a day's itinerary.

id.description: Unique identifier for the activity entity.

dayId.description: Reference to Day. (Relationship: Day 1:N Activity) The ID of the day to which this activity belongs.

cost.description: The estimated cost of the activity.

notes.description: Any notes or remarks about the activity.

aiGenerated.description: Indicates whether the activity was suggested by the AI.

category.description: The category of the activity (e.g., attraction, restaurant).

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support the TravelWise application's core features, focusing on user authentication, trip planning, AI-powered suggestions, and itinerary management. The structure emphasizes authorization independence and efficient data retrieval through denormalization and structural segregation.

**Authorization Independence:**
Authorization is enforced through path-based ownership and membership maps, eliminating the need for `get()` calls in security rules. For example, trips are stored under `/users/{userId}/trips/{tripId}`, making it straightforward to control access based on the `userId`. Collaborative access is managed via the `sharedWith` array in the `Trip` document, effectively denormalizing the user-trip relationship.

**Structural Segregation:**
The structure segregates data based on access requirements. User profiles are stored in `/users/{userId}`, ensuring private access. Public trips are stored under `/users/{userId}/trips/{tripId}`. This segregation allows for simpler and more robust security rules.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
The data structure facilitates secure `list` operations by aligning document paths with authorization requirements. Listing trips under a user's path (`/users/{userId}/trips`) inherently restricts access to only the trips owned or shared with that user. Public trips, if implemented, would reside in a separate collection (e.g., `/public_trips`) to prevent unauthorized access to private trip data during `list` operations.

**Access Modeling:**
- **Private Data:** User profiles are stored using path-based ownership (`/users/{userId}`).
- **User-Owned Data:** Trips are stored under `/users/{userId}/trips/{tripId}`, indicating a one-to-many relationship between users and trips.
- **Collaborative Data:** The `sharedWith` array in the `Trip` document implements a membership model for collaborative access.

This structure enables scalable and maintainable security rules while supporting the application's core features and scalability goals.
